Date of receiving of Appeal : 25.04.2016
 Date of arguments : 25.04.2016

Date of judgment : 26.04.2016
 Judgment

1 By this judgment I will dispose of appeal u/sec.374 Cr.PC. filed on behalf of convict Muni Ram against the judgment dated 07.04.2014 and order on sentence dated 09.04.2014 passed by Sh.
Gaurav Rao, Ld. ACMM-II, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.

2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Singla CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page 1 of 8 Traders at Y-47,
Janta Market, Nangloi, Delhi.

entities.text: Singla CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page 1 of 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On 18.06.2002 at about 4.00 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. V. P. S.
Chaudhary visited the said place and purchased 750 grams of "Dal Arhar" (ready for sale) from accused.
FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. Vijay Khanna.
The said Dal Arhar was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.
As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "the sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz tartrazine."

Sh. Muni Ram S/O Sh. Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139754161/
1 3

entities.text: Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 17.02.2003 with the court.
Accused was summoned.
He has not exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act and get the sample analyzed by CFL.
4 Charge was framed against accused u/sec.2(ia) (a) (j) (m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act.

5 After trial, vide judgment dated 07.04.2014, accused was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act and vide order dated 09.04.2014, accused was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 18 months and fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine SI of 60 days.

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined.
CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page 2 of 8 (ii) Non-compliance of Rule 17 and 18 of PFA Rules i.e. the samples were not properly dispatched to public analyst and the sample seal was not sent.

entities.text: CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, jhawa, polythene were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official.
(iv) The public analyst took about 6 days to sign his report and thus prejudice is caused to the appellant.
(v) Tartrazine colour is permitted in food articles.
(vi) Public analyst was not legally appointed as public analyst on the date of analysis.
7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I have gone through the record, Trial Court record and have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
9 It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public witness was present in the proceedings nor efforts were made and thus compliance of Sec.10 (7) PFA Act was not done.
As far as this argument is concerned, the same argument was raised before the Ld. Trial Court.
The same was dealt by the trial court from para 20 to 25 of the judgment.

As far as opinion/finding of the trial court regarding this argument is concerned, I do not find any infirmity in those findings and the same are upheld and the arguments regarding this fact does not find any force and thus rejected.

Sh. Muni Ram S/O Sh. Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139754161/
2 10

entities.text: Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further argued that there is non-compliance of Rule 17 and 18 of PFA rules i.e. the seal of the samples were not sent separately and not mentioned in the PA Report.
It is further stated that the samples CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page 3 of 8 were not properly dispatched.

entities.text: Muni Ram Vs. State page 3 of 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These facts were also raised before the trial court and are dealt by the trial court from para 102 to 108 in the judgment.

I do not find any different opinion than as stated by the trial court and hence the arguments raised by the the counsel for appellant in this regard are rejected since the same are properly and correctly dealt by the trial court in the findings from para 102 to 108 in the judgment.
11 It is further argued that the PA report was not signed on the same date on which the analysis was done.
It is stated that prejudice had caused to the accused as it caused delay and due to that reason the samples could not be sent for examination for CFL by the accused/appellant.
As far as this argument is concerned, the same does not have any force as the adulteration is on account of "synthetic colour tartrazine".
The said colour/sample is not a perishable item.
So, no prejudice has been caused to the accused/appellant.
Hence, this leg of argument is of no force and thus rejected.
12 It is further stated that the colour used i.e. tartrazine is a permitted colour and thus not covered "added colouring material".
It is further stated that the colour tartrazine is not hazardous to health.
In this regard the arguments were also done before the trial court.
The analysis of these arguments were done before trial court from para 109 to 111 of the judgment.
The reasons given in that part of the judgment does not require interference and thus the arguments addressed by Ld. defence counsel in this regard are rejected.
13 It is further argued that the detection of colour is done by using paper chromatic test and the same is not a reliable test.
Due to that CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page 4 of 8 reason the accused be acquitted.

entities.text: CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This argument was also done by Ld. defence counsel before the trial court and was dealt by the trial court in para 118 of the judgment.

I do not find any any disagreement in the reasoning given by the trial court in this regard and hence the said part of judgment is upheld as correct and the arguments of Ld. defence counsel in this regard are rejected.
14 It is further argued that Smt. Mohini Srivastav was not appointed as public analyst on the day of analysis i.e. 09.07.2002.
However, this part of argument was also done in the lower court and was dealt in para 120 of the judgment.
I do not find to interfere in the findings given in the said paras as the same are correct.
15 It is further argued that compliance u/sec.14(2) PFA Rules was not proved on record by the prosecution.
It is stated that witnesses are deposing differently with respect to the cleanliness of jhaba etc.
It is further stated that it was the duty of the prosecution to prove these facts.
These arguments were also addressed before the trial court.
The relevant part of the judgment dealing with these arguments are from para 26 to 55 of the judgment.
16 Ld.
Trial court while dealing with these arguments had laid stress that the deposition of the PWs was recorded after considerable period of time so certain inconsistencies are bound to come.
It is further stated in the judgment that these discrepancies should be ignored if otherwise, the deposition appears to be not faulty or acceptable.

Sh. Muni Ram S/O Sh. Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139754161/
3 17

entities.text: Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as the arguments in this regard is concerned, the law CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page 5 o discussed by the trial court is correct and the same is self explanatory.

entities.text: CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, as far as the analysis of facts are concerned, to my opinion, the same requires some more elaboration.
As far as Rule 14 of PFA Rules are concerned, it spells out that the FI shall use dry bottles or containers for the purposes of sampling.

However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food.

entities.text: Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis.
So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers".
Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean.

entities.text: Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry.

entities.text:
Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement", it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.

However, it is not the law that the FI shall spell out on CA No.
51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page 6 of 8 which surfaces the sample commodity had touched while sampling.

entities.text:
CA No.
51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, if he chosen to spell out the implements/surfaces with which the sample commodity came into contact/touch, the same must be proved as clean and dry.

19 In the present case, the PW1/FI V. P. S. Chaudhary had not stated anything regarding the involvement of envelop/white paper bag "in examination-in-chief" on which the sample commodity was put before weighing.
However, in his cross-examination dated 19.03.2011 he had stated that the said Dal was put in a white paper bag provided by the vendor.
20 PW3/LHA Vijay Khanna also deposed that Dal was put in one clean and while paper before weighing.

Hence, as per record, there appears that some surface of a article was used by the FI before weighing it on the Pan Scale i.e. white paper bag, but prosecution failed to prove that the said white paper bag was clean and dry.

Sh. Muni Ram S/O Sh. Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139754161/
4

entities.text: Hari Ram vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, in these circumstances, there is non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules and thus the benefit goes in favour of appellant.
21 So, in these circumstances, the judgment and order on sentence of the trial court is reversed.
22 Accused Muni Ram is acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1A) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
23 Bail Bond u/sec.437A Cr.P.C. furnished.
Accepted for six months.
CA No. 51/16 Muni Ram Vs. State page  24 TCR be sent back with copy of the order.
